question: Does the proposed SS OCF 1 Q-ball support a bound, locally readable clock for 100 calibrated periods?

method.action: SS OCF 1 flat decoupling action, U(s)=s-s²+s³, V_chi(s)=0.25-0.4s+0.2s², zeta=0.1; Phi=F(r)exp(-i omega_Q t)u0, a=0.
method.units: c=hbar=m=1, (+---); r and t in m^-1, fields in m, Omega² in m², Q dimensionless.
method.domain: Spherical radius R=80 with h=0.1; trial omega_Q/m=0.868,0.875,0.90,0.94; selected smallest solved bound E/Q<1 candidate.
method.boundaries: Regular r=0, Dirichlet radial u=r Phi and w=r chi at R; outward damping gamma=0.08((r-60)/20)² on momenta in outer layer, logged charge/energy sink. R=160 independent control with sponge at 140.
method.initial_data: Continuous regular BVP with fixed seed radii 5,10,20,40,60 projected by Newton to finite difference grid; chi=A f(r), pi_chi=0, pi_Phi=-i omega_Q Phi, amplitudes A=0,0.0005,0.001,0.002. Deterministic root seed 2026092506 unused by solver.
method.solver: SciPy solve_bvp and tridiagonal discrete Newton; independent symmetric-tridiagonal radial chi eigenproblem and core L+/L- Hessian screen; second-order kick-drift-kick reciprocal Phi/chi evolution. Nominal 100 periods, other amplitudes 20, h/2 and 2R 20.
method.tolerances: Profile residual <2e-10; 5 times eigen error margin; mesh/domain and amplitude frequency <1%; local eigenfrequency agreement <2%; nominal mode-energy loss and charge drift <1%; finite sample crossing count >=99. Resources 650s wall/768MiB/35MiB.

hypotheses.prediction: A positive nodeless core supplies a mode with 0<Omega²<0.25 that ticks locally and retains >99% mode energy and core charge for 100 nominal periods.
No accepted core, no bound mode, unstable core, frequency error or leakage beyond gates prevents a calibrated detector in the tested regime.

controls.purpose: exclude silent phase as local ticking
controls.method: run chi=pi_chi=0 for 20 periods; log local chi and stationary core density/projector
evolve peak chi=0.0005,0.001,0.002, nominal for 100 periods and others for 20
solve profile and spectrum at h/2,R=80 and h,R=160; evolve nominal amplitude for 20 periods on each
